   edits. It fetches, rebases, pushes with one rejection retry and verifies against
   a fresh fetch. Inspect outgoing commits before publishing; coordinate unrelated
   or explicitly held local commits. Verify the operation's commit is included in
   upstream; after a rebase locate it through its unique log path and inspect the
   resulting path membership. Do not delegate publication to Obsidian Git or the user.
   Follow [sync recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md#refused-sync)
   on failure; never force or guess at conflicts. `--commit-local` is for owned hand
   edits outside operations, refuses with any open token, and must not sweep foreign work.

## Combined close and publication

`wiki-sync.mjs --op <token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "<title>"` performs the
same scoped close, then normal sync and remote verification. It closes only the
given token and cannot combine with `--commit-local`. Without an explicit ledger
it uses recorded paths when available, else the guarded unscoped close; prefer an
explicit ledger, especially for file-tool edits. Success distinguishes the landed
commit and publication. A refused close pushes nothing and retains its token;
`committed, not published:` means the close landed and sync still needs recovery.
Inspect state and retry the unfinished step, not the content or log.

**Done only when** the requested change and owned catalogs are validated, one log
and the scoped operation commit are recorded, and remote publication is verified.
Report holds, local-only results and blockers precisely. Detailed verification,
refusal records, uncertain completion, cleanup and Git settings belong to
[operation recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md).

## Exceptions with their own transaction

**Re-clipping:** `apply-reclips.mjs` applies repairs but does not own a commit. Use an enclosing operation with an exact target list and ownership ledger; inspect its returned changed paths. A verified repair, a pending table verification and a quarantine are distinct outcomes. Quarantine may close triage without making evidence citable. See [re-clipping and quarantine](../../../docs/reclipping.md) for selectors, mode overrides and the explicit terminal-failure policy.

- `purge.mjs --apply`, `--restore` and `--reconcile` own their manifests, logs and
  commits. Do not wrap their transaction in a competing commit. Collateral Markdown
  repairs use an ordinary operation after the purge commit. Keep every seed/plan,
  blocking-source and publication safeguard in the purge skill.
- Fresh initialization can open an operation before scaffolding: the helper can create
  its state directory before the other folders exist. Without Git, explicitly report
  local-only initialization; do not manufacture a repository or publish it.
- Starting triage UI only creates machine-local session state; it is not a content
  edit and does not need a commit. Applying dispositions that change tracked vault
  content or pipeline state uses an enclosing or new ordinary operation.

## Executable lifecycle templates

Replace absolute path placeholders, title and narrative with the real task. The
comment marks where the already-authorized edits and checks occur; do not run the
close step after a failed edit/check. These examples assume a configured upstream
and no explicit user hold, so they include the push step. For an explicit local-only
request, omit that step and report the unpushed commit. The close is scoped with
`--paths-file`; to close and publish in one command, replace the `op-commit` and

# Vault schema (wiki-master)

This vault is an LLM-maintained wiki (Karpathy pattern). Maintained by the
`wiki-master` Claude Code plugin.

## Layout
- `raw/` — captured sources. The **content is never modified**: no LLM rewriting, no
  reinterpreting what a source said — that integrity is the whole point of provenance.
  Deterministic tooling may still perform *faithful* representation transforms that preserve
  the content — text extraction, localizing an image reference to a stored copy, pipeline-state
  frontmatter. The line is semantic (never alter the evidence), not byte-level (freeze the file).
  `raw/clippings/` — Web Clipper / clip.mjs output. `raw/attachments/` — downloaded assets,
  content-hash named.
- `wiki/sources|entities|concepts|syntheses|authored` — LLM-owned pages. Under
  `wiki/authored/`, a page belonging to a multi-doc project lives at
  `wiki/authored/<project>/[<subproject>/]<file>.md` — see the Frontmatter contract
  below for the `project`/`kind` fields that drive this, and
  `skills/wiki-project/references/authoring.md` for the canonical per-kind placement table
  ("write a user guide" always resolves to `<project>/guides/user.md`, etc.).
- `moc/` — Maps of Content. `index.md` — catalog. `log/` — one file per operation, viewed via `log.base`.
- `.recycle/` — purged topics, one folder per purge with a `manifest.json` recording what
  moved (by path and by `source-hash`) and which source URLs were declined. Git-tracked, so a
  removal reaches every machine; dot-prefixed, so no search, metric or graph walk ever sees it.
  Never emptied automatically — a purge is reversible, and that is what makes it safe to run.

## Frontmatter contract
- Raw/clippings: `title, source, author, published, created, tags:[clippings], quality, topic, source-hash`.
  `topic` records the research topic the clipping was gathered for (the argument given to
  `wiki-researcher` discovery); it is omitted for clips made outside a research run, and it is what the
  triage queue groups by.
- Wiki pages: `type, created, updated, reviewed, status, sources:["[[...]]"], ai-generated`.
  Source pages also carry `source-hashes:[<sha256>,…]` — the `source-hash` of each
  clipping they summarize; this is the content key the ingest-backlog metric joins on.
  `wiki/authored/` pages additionally carry optional `project` (a slug, one `/` deep
  at most for a sub-project) and `kind` (`overview|architecture|reference|guide|
  diagram|decision|roadmap|note|backlog-item`) — grouping metadata a per-project MOC
  generator reads; a `kind: decision` page also carries `decision-status`
  (`proposed|accepted|superseded|deprecated`), and a `kind: backlog-item` page
  carries `backlog-status` (`planned|in-progress|shipped|blocked|dropped`) — one
  small file per tracked item, edited in place as status changes rather than
  accumulating appended "Update (date): ..." paragraphs. A backlog item may also
  carry `depends-on`, a list of quoted wikilinks to other backlog items of the same
  project; it never changes the item's own status.

## Rules

### Identity, relationships and verification

Concepts may carry `aliases: ["equivalent name"]` and a one-sentence `scope:`.
Search existing titles/aliases and neighboring concepts before creating a new one.
Different scopes remain distinct pages; aliases do not mean broader or related.
Use full-path links whenever a basename or alias is ambiguous.

Keep supporting citations in `sources:` and factual prose. Put navigation in
`## Relationships` or `Related:`, with an explanatory sentence and a small role
vocabulary: broader, narrower, prerequisite, complements, alternative, contrasts,
applies-to. Navigation does not make the destination supporting evidence.

`reviewed` records factual verification. `updated` records edits. Mechanical
changes preserve `reviewed`; missing review means unverified. Index freshness
is a third, independent state. MOCs route tasks through prerequisites, alternatives,
complementary topics and evidence; generated project catalogs are separate from
curated task maps. See `_templates/concept-note.md` and `_templates/task-map.md`.
- Raw is the source of truth. Every wiki page cites its `raw/` provenance —
  **except** `wiki/authored/`: original, primary content (advisory documentation,
  policy, house style) written directly into the wiki, not derived from a
  captured source. These pages declare the exception explicitly (`sources: []`)
  rather than by omission; they are living pages like any other `wiki/` page,
  never requiring a `raw/` counterpart.
- Links are `[[wikilinks]]`; embeds `![[...]]` are transclusion only.

## Git ownership

The plugin's scripts make the scoped commits and the sync: `op-commit` commits what one
operation wrote, and `wiki-sync.mjs` pulls, rebases and pushes. Obsidian Git stays installed for its
source-control view and for pulling, with auto-commit, commit on file change and auto-push
all off. An instruction anywhere else that says otherwise is stale.

# Validate exactly the task paths

Before committing, check exactly the pages the task wrote:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/validate-authored.mjs" --paths-file <ledger>`,
with the vault set through [access](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md).
This procedure is read-only. A validation-only request opens no operation and makes
no edits, logs or catalog refreshes. For supplied paths, place a JSON ledger outside
the vault; an existing authoring operation may use its recorded ledger.

**The ledger** is the file `op-commit.mjs --paths-file` takes: a non-empty JSON array
of vault-relative paths with `/` separators (no drive prefix, backslash, empty segment,
`.` or `..`), for example `["wiki/authored/demo/guides/user.md","wiki/authored/demo/roadmap.md"]`.
Record each page you wrote with `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token> <path>...` (the log and
catalog scripts record theirs when given `--since`), then
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" show --since <token> --out <ledger>`
writes this file and lists on stderr what the close would get wrong (a path that was already
dirty before `op-begin`, a path that is not dirty now, a changed path nobody recorded). Writing
it by hand with your file tool still works. Keep it under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. A path with no file at that exact spelling is reported as `missing-file`: a page that
does not exist, or one whose letter case or Unicode form differs from the file on disk,
because a case-insensitive disk would otherwise drop that page's link checks without a word.

**The result.** The command writes nothing and reads the whole vault (ambiguity is
vault-wide), but reports only ledger pages; `health.mjs` stays the whole-vault check.
Exit 0 is clean, 1 means defects (fix and rerun), 2 means an unusable ledger, unknown
flag or missing vault. The text report is one `path:line rule message` line per defect,
sorted by path then line, then `validate-authored: N pages checked, M defects`, with
`, K skipped` appended only when K is above zero (checked plus skipped is the number of
distinct ledger paths). `--json` prints
`{"version":1,"checked":N,"skipped":K,"defects":[{"path","line","rule","message"}]}`
instead, which is exactly what `validateAuthored()` in `scripts/validate-authored.mjs` returns. An absent frontmatter key is reported at line 1; a blank key at its own line.

**Public pages.** A page written for a plugin's public repository must not name other projects or machines. `--terms-file <path>` (the owner's private list, kept outside every repository; the file `scripts/scan-private-terms.mjs` reads) adds a `private-term` defect for each ledger page whose text matches a term or a built-in machine pattern (a home-directory path, a GPU model, an invisible character), at its line, naming the rule number and never the text. `--terms-projects a,b` limits the check to pages whose `project:` (first segment) is listed, so a private project's own pages may name themselves. Without `--terms-file` the output is unchanged.

Under `wiki/authored/`:

- `missing-key`: `type`, `created`, `updated`, `status`, `ai-generated` and a
  `sources` line (`[]` is valid) must be present and not blank, so an unfilled
  template fails. A page in a project folder also needs `project` and `kind`, a
  decision `decision-status`, a backlog item `backlog-status`. `reviewed` is optional.

# Preview, purge or restore a topic

Remove only the approved topic and its evidence closure, preserving collateral
knowledge and recoverability. Selecting this skill is not approval to apply or
publish a removal. Purge owns its transaction; do not wrap it in an ordinary one.

## Workflow

1. Read [purge procedure](references/purge.md),
   [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md),
   [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) and
   [operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md). Resolve the
   intended vault and open applicable instructions. Confirm preview, apply,
   restore or authorized reconciliation scope.
2. Before mutation, check [actual history connectivity](../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md#purge-history-connectivity) and retain the
   [broken-link baseline](../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#purge-broken-link-verification).
   Missing coverage/upstream differs from unrelated histories; never guess a new
   remote or canonical history. Preview-only requests do not run mutating reconciliation.
3. Generate the plan, inspect every seed and search coverage, pin corrected seeds,
   then present layer counts, collateral and blocking pages for explicit approval.
   Resolve blocking dependencies before applying. A relevance score is not consent.
4. Apply only the approved plan with the same pinned seeds. The helper owns
   manifest, moves, declines, log and commit. Repair authorized collateral in a
   separate scoped relink operation; [validate changed paths](../wiki-setup/references/validation.md).
   Hold both commits until explicit publication approval, then sync and verify.
5. Verify the broken-link count did not grow and report the transaction ID,
   actual moved/restored/skipped/missing paths and publication state. If interrupted,
   follow [recovery](../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md#interrupted-purge)
   for the same transaction instead of applying another empty plan.

## Examples

- **Preview:** Request: “Show what removing the obsolete Beacon topic would affect.”
  Action: run `purge.mjs --plan "Beacon"`, inspect matched pages and produce a
  pinned plan if necessary. Result: proposed removals and named collateral/blockers;
  no reconciliation, moves, operation, log or commit.
- **Approved removal:** Request: “Apply that reviewed plan.” Action: use the same
  seeds, repair authorized collateral and compare broken-link counts. Result:
  a reversible local purge transaction; ask for publication approval if it has
  not already been explicitly supplied.
- **Restore:** Request: “Restore purge `<id>`.” Action: run
  `purge.mjs --restore <id>` and inspect every skipped or missing entry.
  Result: restored files without overwriting newer work; report partial restoration
  honestly and honor the transaction's publication authorization.
- **Reconcile:** Request: “Finish the interrupted purge `<id>`.” Action: inspect
  the saved transaction through the linked recovery procedure and run the
  authorized reconciliation. Result: the original purge is completed or an exact
  blocker remains; a second empty purge is never substituted.

## Best practices

Never hard-delete the recycle bin or use its contents as evidence. Review seeds
by content, not ranking. A better health score does not prove collateral repair;
compare broken-link counts. Preserve newer files on restore, and never turn
missing capture/search coverage into a claim that a topic does not exist.

## Advanced references

The [complete purge procedure](references/purge.md) owns apply/restore approval
and transaction semantics. Setup owns [checks](../wiki-setup/references/checks.md),
[search diagnostics](../wiki-setup/references/search-diagnostics.md) and
[interrupted recovery](../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md#interrupted-purge).
Use [maintainer repair](../wiki-maintainer/references/repair.md) for authorized collateral.

## Done

A preview has a reviewed, scoped plan and no mutation. An applied/restored
transaction is verified, collateral is accounted for, and publication is either
explicitly approved and verified or truthfully held/local-only. Missing files,
unrelated history or an incomplete transaction are reported as blockers.

5

9	
10	1. **An uncommitted deletion.** A removal that never becomes a commit is not a
11	   removal anything else can see; the next sync undoes it. Purge owns its whole
12	   transaction through commit, so this one is closed by construction.
13	2. **A `raw/` clipping left behind.** The ingest backlog reports it as

15	   from evidence nobody removed.
16	3. **A source URL nobody declined.** Researcher discovery re-finds and re-clips it.
17	4. **A removal committed onto a history this clone cannot reach.** This is the
18	   failure that purge cannot detect. A

first three in one transaction, and `--reconcile` closes them again on every other
machine. **It cannot close the fourth** — recognizing that one is on you.

1. **An uncommitted deletion.** A removal that never becomes a commit is not a
   removal anything else can see; the next sync undoes it. Purge owns its whole
   transaction through commit, so this one is closed by construction.
2. **A `raw/` clipping left behind.** The ingest backlog reports it as
   un-summarized forever, and the next researcher ingestion faithfully rebuilds the topic
   from evidence nobody removed.
3. **A source URL nobody declined.** Researcher discovery re-finds and re-clips it.
4. **A removal committed onto a history this clone cannot reach.** This is the
   failure that purge cannot detect. A
   force-push or filter-branch rewrite gives origin a new lineage; a clone that
   never pulls it keeps the old one — every removed file still present — and
   auto-sync can keep committing to it. When the lineages have **no merge base**,
   the clone can retain every removed file even though the remote records removal.

**Check before mutation:** follow the direct [history-connectivity diagnostic](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md#purge-history-connectivity). Stop on confirmed unrelated histories. A missing upstream/fetch failure is a distinct condition; non-Git work is local-only. Choosing a canonical history is not a purge decision.

## Steps

1. **Establish the baseline; reconcile only when authorized.**
   Follow the direct [broken-link verification procedure](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#purge-broken-link-verification) before any mutation and retain its initial count. For a preview-only request, do not reconcile: proceed directly to the read-only plan. When completing an explicitly authorized prior removal, use [interrupted-purge recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md#interrupted-purge); reconciliation moves files and commits, even when it is silent on a clean vault.

2. **Plan.**
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/purge.mjs" --plan "<topic>"`
   Moves nothing. Prints the seeds it matched, every file it would bin, and two
   lists that need a human decision:
   - **COLLATERAL** — pages that survive but link into the purge set. Their
     references need repairing in step 4.
   - **BLOCKING** — pages whose every cited source is inside the set. `--apply`
     refuses while any exist. Either add them to the purge or keep their sources;
     a claim with no evidence is a defect (guardrail #2), so purge will not decide
     this silently in either direction.

3. **Check the seeds before the plan, then get explicit approval.** Never skip
   either half.

   **Read the seed list first.** Search ranks by relevance but has no notion of
   "relevant enough" — the scores come from RRF fusion and carry no absolute
   meaning, so the tail of a ranked seed list can drift into adjacent topics, and
   every off-topic seed drags its exclusive evidence into the bin with it.
   Inspect the actual pages; topical similarity alone does not authorize removal.

   Strike anything that does not belong and re-run pinned:
   `--plan "<topic>" --seeds "wiki/concepts/A.md,wiki/concepts/B.md"`
   Paths are vault-relative and validated — a typo is refused rather than silently narrowing
   the purge.

   **Then read the plan back** grouped by layer with counts, naming the collateral
   and blocking pages specifically, and get an explicit yes. Purge moves many files
   at once and the closure reaches further than expected when a topic is densely
   linked.

4. **Apply** — with the same `--seeds` you approved, if you pinned any.
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/purge.mjs" --apply "<topic>" [--seeds "..."]`
   Writes the manifest, moves the files, records declines, writes the log entry, and
   commits — staging only what the purge touched, never the user's unrelated work.
   Then:
   - open an ordinary relink operation before repairing references on every
     COLLATERAL page (the log entry lists them);
   - regenerate the catalog: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/index-gen.mjs"`;
   - [validate changed paths](../../wiki-setup/references/validation.md), log and close that repair operation through the shared contract,
     preserving already-dirty files. Never `git add -A`. The purge transaction
     itself already owns its commit and must not be wrapped in a competing one.
     Defer publication of both commits until the explicit push approval in step 5.

5. **Ask before pushing.** A push publishes the removal to every machine. Ask
   plainly — "publish this purge to the configured upstream?" — and only on a
   yes run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs"` and verify remote
   publication through the shared completion contract. If the vault is not a Git
   repo, say plainly that the purge is local and will not reach other copies.

6. **Verify — on the broken-link count, not the score.**
   Repeat the direct [broken-link check](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#purge-broken-link-verification) and compare with the saved baseline. The count must not have grown. Inspect collateral and report actual publication state; a better score never proves a safe purge.

## When a purge stops partway

Use [interrupted-purge recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md#interrupted-purge) to inspect and finish the same authorized transaction. Do not rerun `--apply` as a substitute; preserve its original manifest, scope and publication boundary.

## Restoring

`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/purge.mjs" --restore <purge-id>` puts everything
back and commits.

- It never overwrites a file already at the original path — that is newer work, and
  it is reported as **skipped** instead.
- It clears the declines this purge recorded, so researcher discovery can find those
  sources again. Declines made for other reasons are left alone.
- Anything the manifest claims but the bin cannot supply is reported as **MISSING**
  with a non-zero exit. **Never read a bare `restored N file(s)` as success** without
  checking that line.

## Rules

- **Never read, cite, or count `.recycle/`.** It is excluded from every metric and
  every search by design — `graph.mjs` skips dot-prefixed entries during its walk,
  supported readers exclude that scope. A page in the bin is not evidence, not a
  source, and not backlog.
- **Never hard-delete the bin.** Retention is deliberate and unbounded: purge is
  reversible, and that is the only reason it is safe to run at all.
- **Never `--apply` without showing the plan and getting approval first.**
- **Never `git add -A` in a vault.** Stage the paths the operation touched. The
  vault carries the user's in-progress writing, and a commit that sweeps it up is
  both mislabelled and impossible to revert cleanly.
- **An empty result is not an answer.** If `--plan` reports no wiki pages for a
  topic, inspect its search diagnostics: the helper refuses to trust an empty
  result when the primary wiki keyword scan failed. Do not reinterpret unavailable
  coverage as "this topic does not exist"; use [search diagnostics](../../wiki-setup/references/search-diagnostics.md) when needed. Healthy search still requires reviewing
  seeds for relevance; it does not authorize applying a plan.

# Discover, capture and ingest evidence

Keep the source set and authorized outcome explicit. Candidates-only discovery
is read-only; capture-only creates raw evidence, never derived pages. An
unspecified request to use this role does not authorize processing the backlog.

## Workflow

1. Read [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), resolve the known vault
   and absolute installed helpers, and open applicable vault instructions.
   Choose discovery, named capture, named ingestion or default-backlog ingestion
   from the request. Clarify an ambiguous task before writing.
2. Follow the corresponding direct procedure below. Discovery requires separate
   read-only finders and independent selection when delegation is available;
   retain that selection before capture. Named sources skip broad discovery.

## Modes and examples

- **Discover:** read [discovery](references/discover.md).
  Request: “Find evidence on retry budgets; return candidates only.” Action:
  check coverage/dedup, dispatch five perspective finders and independently select
  their candidates. Result: a justified source list without clips, declines or logs.
  An explicit discover-and-capture/ingest request can continue within that scope.
- **Named URL or saved page:** read [capture](references/capture.md).
  Request: “Capture this saved article.” Action: use `clip.mjs --from-file` for
  the named URL, preserving dedup, declines and provenance. Result: a verified
  raw clipping and completed operation; no source summary unless ingestion was requested.
- **Format or service capture:** read the matching complete route:
  [PDF](references/clip-pdf.md), [Word](references/clip-docx.md),
  [PowerPoint](references/clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheets](references/clip-xlsx.md),
  [GitHub repository](references/clip-gh.md), or [Confluence](references/clip-confluence.md).
  Request: “Clip this PDF with its figures.” Action: run its linked prerequisite
  check, then `clip-pdf.mjs --figures` inside the owned operation and inspect the
  returned text/images. Result: citable capture paths with actual fidelity limits.
  Other formats use their named helper, never an improvised raw file.
- **Named ingestion:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md).
  Request: “Ingest these two clippings.” Action: read exactly those sources,
  exclude restricted or already-summarized hashes, then write only supported
  source/concept changes. Result: summaries with exact raw paths and source hashes.
- **Default backlog ingestion:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md) and the
  [hash-join contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md).
  Request: “Process new clippings.” Action: obtain the
  [backlog report](../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog), then
  inspect eligibility. Result: only eligible sources are ingested; already summarized
  sources stay unchanged and restricted sources are reported separately. If none
  remain, make no pages, operation, log, commit or index refresh.

## Best practices

Prefer named source sets and coordinate shared concept/catalog edits. A capture's
fidelity and its author's credibility are different judgments. Do not invent
text when tools or authenticated access are unavailable. Source count is not a
quality target. Do not treat a backlog count as ingestion authorization.

## Advanced references

Load the exact [capture prerequisite section](../wiki-setup/references/capture-prerequisites.md)
the selected format requires. Tool trouble uses that same section; operation
failure uses [recovery](../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md). Concept
identity, evidence and transaction rules remain in the directly linked shared
contracts; original project documentation belongs to [wiki-project](../wiki-project/SKILL.md).

## Done

The requested candidates, captures or eligible ingestion set are accounted for,
fidelity/exclusions/coverage are honest, and all authorized mutations have exact
ledgers and verified completion. A requested retrieval handoff actually ran.
Candidates-only and zero-eligible ingestion leave the vault unchanged.

If the text is new it writes a second clipping beside the first, named as the oldest capture's own name followed by ` (recaptured YYYY-MM-DD)`, with the same suffix on its `title`, `recapture-of` naming the newest existing capture, and `created` today; the older clipping is never edited. A second recapture on the same day with different text is a `clash`. `--slug=<name>` with `--recapture` is used exactly, with no suffix. Without the flag the same URL is a `duplicate`.

**A page a person saved.** `clip.mjs "<url>" --from-file <path> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>` records a page saved from a signed-in browser, with its real URL as `source` and nothing fetched. The file is `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt` (the page text) or `.html` or `.htm` (read by the same extractor as a fetched page), at most 1 MiB. The clipping carries `extraction: manual` and `supplied-sha256`, the SHA-256 of the file's bytes; the file's name is not recorded. The ordinary thin, interstitial and decline checks still apply; inspect the actual result and [supplied-page diagnosis](../../wiki-setup/references/capture-prerequisites.md#html-and-supplied-pages). `--from-file` on an existing URL is a duplicate; adding `--recapture` requests a dated new capture. Refresh an `extraction: manual` clipping through this same supplied-file route, not `apply-reclips`. These interfaces do not authorize inventing the page body.

**Names.** A page's title names its file. A document with no title and no heading is named from its URL path, nearest folder first, so `.../skills/one/SKILL.md` is `one-SKILL.md` and `.../skills/two/SKILL.md` is `two-SKILL.md`; the bare last segment is used only after the folders. The frontmatter `title:` stays exactly what the extractor returned, so `title: ""` on such a clipping is not a defect. A new clipping never ends `.md.md`; an older one may, and its name is still valid. A title another clipping already holds gets the distinguishing URL part added, for example `Smith v. Jones (93-1260.ZO)`. `--slug=<name>` chooses the file name without `.md`; a taken name is a clash and is never suffixed. `clip-pdf`, `clip-docx`, `clip-pptx` and `clip-xlsx` also take `--title="<text>"`, for a file whose name is not its title (`valve.pdf`), and `--slug=<name>`.

An option a clipper does not know exits 2 with its usage and clips nothing; `--help` prints the usage and clips nothing.

**Every unresolved link is queued for triage automatically.** `clip.mjs` records
`failed`, `thin`, and `wrong-node` outcomes to `.wiki-master/triage.jsonl`, so a
link that needs a human survives the terminal scrollback. Do not rely on your
completion report to carry them — point the user at [maintainer triage](../../wiki-maintainer/references/triage.md), where they can
disposition each one (retry, decline, clipped-by-hand). Queue anything else that
needs their judgement yourself with `recordIssue(vaultPath, { url, kind:
'attention', reason })`.

2	
3	For a requested research → ingest → search-and-answer flow, complete ingestion
4	below and then follow [wiki-search](../../wiki-search/SKILL.md),
5	[advanced retrieval](../../wiki-search/references/advanced.md) when needed, and
6	[cited answers](../../wiki-search/references/answers.md). Run the search helper against the
7	updated vault before answering and inspect returned passages and exact evidence.
8	Lexical search works without a semantic index. Report unavailable channels;
9	reading the pages you just wrote does not replace the requested retrieval step.
10	Ordinary ingestion alone does not require this additional answer workflow.
11	
12	Read [access and host commands](../../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md) before touching the vault. Also read for this operation: [evidence](../../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md).
13	Load the rest only when this run reaches it — [efficacy](../../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md) before creating or merging a concept, alias or relationship; [maintenance](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md) when you compute the backlog with the content-hash join, or hit a structural repair.
14	Before the first authorized write, follow the shared operations completion contract; reuse existing session authorization.
15	
16	## Select eligible work before opening an operation
17	
18	For an explicit request to process new/un-ingested clippings without a filename,
19	run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs" --backlog` through the direct
20	[backlog check](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog). The **not ingested
21	(no summary records their hash)** list is the starting set. This source-hash join,
22	including its documented legacy fallback, is authoritative for membership; do
23	not infer backlog from filenames, navigation citations or a successful exit.
24	An unspecified request to use the researcher role is not a request to ingest all.
25	
26	For named clippings, resolve and read those exact paths only. Check the same
27	hash-join report and the existing source summaries before doing work: if a source
28	page already records that clipping's `source-hash`, preserve it and report already
29	ingested. A rerun creates no duplicate summary or unearned second ingestion.
30	An explicit request to revise an existing summary can update that canonical page;
31	do not expand named ingestion to unrelated backlog or broad discovery.
32	
33	Inspect each selected clipping's metadata before treating it as support. Exclude
34	`citation-status: quarantined`, `restricted` or `retired` evidence, preserving its
35	raw bytes and restriction; report it separately rather than summarizing it as
36	accepted support. A missing source hash is a repair issue, not permission to
37	invent one. Binary originals and figure sidecars are not summary targets. The
38	helper's backlog can include restricted or defective captures, so its count is
39	not automatically the count of eligible work.
40	
41	If the backlog is zero, every named source is already summarized, or no eligible
42	source remains, stop and report the actual result and any exclusions. Do not
43	create pages, open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes. For work that
44	remains, retain the exact eligible set and initial hash-join membership. See
45	[backlog semantics](../../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md) for migration
46	and repair cases; structural repair still needs its own authorized scope.
47	
48	## Ingest and complete the selected set
49	
50	Read [operation completion](../../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md)
51	before the first authorized write.
52	
53	**Open the operation first:** `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op ingest`
54	This records what was already uncommitted, so the commit at the end contains your
55	work and not the user's in-progress writing. Close it in step 6.
56	
57	**Keep the ledger as you go.** Record each page you write (`wiki/sources/...`, a concept
58	or synthesis you create or change) with
59	`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" add --since <token> <path>...`, and give

# Discover, capture and ingest evidence

Keep the source set and authorized outcome explicit. Candidates-only discovery
is read-only; capture-only creates raw evidence, never derived pages. An
unspecified request to use this role does not authorize processing the backlog.

## Workflow

1. Read [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), resolve the known vault
   and absolute installed helpers, and open applicable vault instructions.
   Choose discovery, named capture, named ingestion or default-backlog ingestion
   from the request. Clarify an ambiguous task before writing.
2. Follow the corresponding direct procedure below. Discovery requires separate
   read-only finders and independent selection when delegation is available;
   retain that selection before capture. Named sources skip broad discovery.
   Ingestion determines eligibility before opening any operation.
3. Read [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before judging
   fidelity or synthesizing. Preserve raw bodies, exact hashes and paths,
   restricted-source exclusions and separate Reddit/Medium sections. Before an
   authorized write, read [operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md),
   open or reuse its token, and record every written path.
4. Capture with the matching helper; pass the same research topic and `--since`
   token throughout a run. Ingest only the authorized eligible set, reuse
   canonical pages and explain useful relationships under the
   [identity contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md).
5. Verify capture fidelity or derived claims, refresh affected owned catalogs and
   log once. Before closing any ingestion, export and inspect its actual owned-path
   ledger, then run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/validate-authored.mjs" --paths-file <ledger>`
   using the direct [scoped validation procedure](../wiki-setup/references/validation.md).
   Require exit 0 before commit/sync; a health, lint or backlog report does not
   replace this validation. Then complete scoped publication unless held.
6. If the request continues with a search or answer, load
   [wiki-search](../wiki-search/SKILL.md) and actually run retrieval against the
   updated vault, opening its returned passages. Use
   [advanced retrieval](../wiki-search/references/advanced.md) or
   [cited answers](../wiki-search/references/answers.md) as needed. Memory of pages
   just written is not retrieval; lexical-only availability is disclosed, not a
   reason to skip this step. The answer stays read-only unless filing is authorized.

## Modes and examples

- **Discover:** read [discovery](references/discover.md).
  Request: “Find evidence on retry budgets; return candidates only.” Action:
  check coverage/dedup, dispatch five perspective finders and independently select
  their candidates. Result: a justified source list without clips, declines or logs.
  An explicit discover-and-capture/ingest request can continue within that scope.
- **Named URL or saved page:** read [capture](references/capture.md).
  Request: “Capture this saved article.” Action: use `clip.mjs --from-file` for
  the named URL, preserving dedup, declines and provenance. Result: a verified
  raw clipping and completed operation; no source summary unless ingestion was requested.
- **Format or service capture:** read the matching complete route:
  [PDF](references/clip-pdf.md), [Word](references/clip-docx.md),
  [PowerPoint](references/clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheets](references/clip-xlsx.md),
  [GitHub repository](references/clip-gh.md), or [Confluence](references/clip-confluence.md).
  Request: “Clip this PDF with its figures.” Action: run its linked prerequisite
  check, then `clip-pdf.mjs --figures` inside the owned operation and inspect the
  returned text/images. Result: citable capture paths with actual fidelity limits.
  Other formats use their named helper, never an improvised raw file.
- **Named ingestion:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md).
  Request: “Ingest these two clippings.” Action: read exactly those sources,
  exclude restricted or already-summarized hashes, then write only supported
  source/concept changes. Result: summaries with exact raw paths and source hashes.
- **Default backlog ingestion:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md) and the
  [hash-join contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md).
  Request: “Process new clippings.” Action: obtain the
  [backlog report](../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog), then
  inspect eligibility. Result: only eligible sources are ingested; already summarized
  sources stay unchanged and restricted sources are reported separately. If none
  remain, make no pages, operation, log, commit or index refresh.

## Best practices

Prefer named source sets and coordinate shared concept/catalog edits. A capture's
fidelity and its author's credibility are different judgments. Do not invent
text when tools or authenticated access are unavailable. Source count is not a
quality target. Do not treat a backlog count as ingestion authorization.

## Advanced references

Load the exact [capture prerequisite section](../wiki-setup/references/capture-prerequisites.md)
the selected format requires. Tool trouble uses that same section; operation
failure uses [recovery](../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md). Concept
identity, evidence and transaction rules remain in the directly linked shared
contracts; original project documentation belongs to [wiki-project](../wiki-project/SKILL.md).

## Done

The requested candidates, captures or eligible ingestion set are accounted for,
fidelity/exclusions/coverage are honest, and all authorized mutations have exact
ledgers and verified completion. A requested retrieval handoff actually ran.
Candidates-only and zero-eligible ingestion leave the vault unchanged.

21	[operation recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md) for details.

This is the single shared transaction contract for ordinary authorized vault
writes: capture, ingestion, original authoring, content repair, synthesis filing
and applied triage dispositions. Read-only search, answers, checks and previews
open no operations, logs, commits or refreshes. Purge retains its separate plan
and publication approvals and owns its transaction.

## Ownership and authorization

An authorized wiki edit includes scoped validation, catalog maintenance, log,
commit, sync and verified remote publication unless the user explicitly holds it.
Finish those steps without another routine permission question. Never create a
remote/repository just to satisfy publication. Without an upstream report local-only;
a local commit or closed token alone is not publication.

Read vault instructions. Preserve foreign edits and immutable raw bodies. A token
snapshots existing dirty paths, not later ownership, and does not isolate edits to
the same file. Coordinate overlapping targets. On resumption reconcile the saved
token, owned paths, log and actual commit before opening another operation; use
[operation recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md) for details.
Never delete a token or Git lock to hide unfinished work.

An enclosing operation may own delegated work. Give the worker that token; it
records exact paths and validation, never closes or aborts the parent's operation.
The named owner remains responsible for scoped publication. Do not close user-held
or foreign tokens. If blocked, retain actual state and a durable handoff naming
the token, owned files, completed steps, unfinished work and exact next action.

## Ordinary lifecycle

1. **Open before the first write.** Run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op <op>` and retain the token.
   Create new pages only afterward. Use the existing operation vocabulary:
   original project documentation uses `relink`; derived answer filing uses `query`;
   discovery, ingestion, lint and relink retain their task operations.
2. **Keep an exact ledger.** Pass `--since <token>` to clippers, `log-entry.mjs`,
   `index-gen.mjs` and applied `refresh-catalogs.mjs` so they record actual written
   paths. Record file-tool edits with
   `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token> <vault-relative-path>...`. Use
   `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>` to produce the JSON array for
   `--paths-file`, under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. Inspect its warnings:
   pre-dirty recorded paths, paths no longer dirty and changed but unrecorded paths.
   Do not rebuild the ledger from Git's quoted filename display: Unicode paths
   can be silently lost. Unclaimed files are not automatically yours.
3. **Edit and validate.** Check behavior, schema, canonical placement and exact
   citations. Follow direct [scoped validation](../../wiki-setup/references/validation.md)
   for changed pages and the relevant [checks](../../wiki-setup/references/checks.md).
   Advance `reviewed` only after factual verification; mechanical edits preserve it.
   Inspect an uncertain write's actual target before retrying. A failed check
   stops completion until its cause is resolved within scope.
4. **Refresh affected owned catalogs once.** Generated fences are derived, never
   hand-edited. `index-gen.mjs` regenerates the global index while preserving manual
   framing. Project documentation uses [project catalogs](../../wiki-project/references/catalogs.md).
   A catalog already dirty from another writer remains theirs: use safe project
   generators and report deferred global refresh. Record actual changed paths,
   rebuild the ledger and rerun validation when the owned set grows.
5. **Log once.** Pipe a concise narrative to
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/log-entry.mjs" --op <op> --title "<title>" --since <token>`.
   The helper creates one unique `log/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss-<op>-<slug>.md` with
   date/op/title metadata and records its path. Never append to an aggregate log.
6. **Commit and inspect.** Regenerate the ledger and read its warnings, then run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op <op> --title "<title>" --since <token> --paths-file <ledger>`.

7. **Sync and verify.** `op-commit` never pushes. Run
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs"` after closing, not between
   edits. It fetches, rebases, pushes with one rejection retry and verifies against

## Combined close and publication

`wiki-sync.mjs --op <token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "<title>"` performs the
same scoped close, then normal sync and remote verification. It closes only the
given token and cannot combine with `--commit-local`. Without an explicit ledger
it uses recorded paths when available, else the guarded unscoped close; prefer an
explicit ledger, especially for file-tool edits. Success distinguishes the landed
commit and publication. A refused close pushes nothing and retains its token;
`committed, not published:` means the close landed and sync still needs recovery.
Inspect state and retry the unfinished step, not the content or log.

**Done only when** the requested change and owned catalogs are validated, one log
and the scoped operation commit are recorded, and remote publication is verified.
Report holds, local-only results and blockers precisely. Detailed verification,
refusal records, uncertain completion, cleanup and Git settings belong to
[operation recovery](../../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md).

## Exceptions with their own transaction

**Re-clipping:** `apply-reclips.mjs` applies repairs but does not own a commit. Use an enclosing operation with an exact target list and ownership ledger; inspect its returned changed paths. $wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'

  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not log wiki operation' }
  $wikiLedger = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "wiki-ledger-$wikiOpToken.json"
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-ledger.mjs' show --since $wikiOpToken --out $wikiLedger

}

# Discover, capture and ingest evidence

Keep the source set and authorized outcome explicit. Candidates-only discovery
is read-only; capture-only creates raw evidence, never derived pages. An
unspecified request to use this role does not authorize processing the backlog.

## Workflow

1. Read [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), resolve the known vault
   and absolute installed helpers, and open applicable vault instructions.
   Choose discovery, named capture, named ingestion or default-backlog ingestion
   from the request. Clarify an ambiguous task before writing.
2. Follow the corresponding direct procedure below. Discovery requires separate
   read-only finders and independent selection when delegation is available;
   retain that selection before capture. Named sources skip broad discovery.
   Ingestion determines eligibility before opening any operation.
3. Read [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before judging
   fidelity or synthesizing. Preserve raw bodies, exact hashes and paths,
   restricted-source exclusions and separate Reddit/Medium sections. Before an
   authorized write, read [operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md),
   open or reuse its token, and record every written path.
4. Capture with the matching helper; pass the same research topic and `--since`
   token throughout a run. Ingest only the authorized eligible set, reuse
   canonical pages and explain useful relationships under the
   [identity contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md).
5. Verify capture fidelity or derived claims, refresh affected owned catalogs and
   log once. Before closing any ingestion, export and inspect its actual owned-path
   ledger, then run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/validate-authored.mjs" --paths-file <ledger>`
   using the direct [scoped validation procedure](../wiki-setup/references/validation.md).
   Require exit 0 before commit/sync; a health, lint or backlog report does not
   replace this validation. Then complete scoped publication unless held.
6. If the request continues with a search or answer, load
   [wiki-search](../wiki-search/SKILL.md) and actually run retrieval against the
   updated vault, opening its returned passages. Use
   [advanced retrieval](../wiki-search/references/advanced.md) or
   [cited answers](../wiki-search/references/answers.md) as needed. Memory of pages
   just written is not retrieval; lexical-only availability is disclosed, not a
   reason to skip this step. The answer stays read-only unless filing is authorized.

## Modes and examples

- **Discover:** read [discovery](references/discover.md).
  Request: “Find evidence on retry budgets; return candidates only.” Action:
  check coverage/dedup, dispatch five perspective finders and independently select
  their candidates. Result: a justified source list without clips, declines or logs.
  An explicit discover-and-capture/ingest request can continue within that scope.
- **Named URL or saved page:** read [capture](references/capture.md).
  Request: “Capture this saved article.” Action: use `clip.mjs --from-file` for
  the named URL, preserving dedup, declines and provenance. Result: a verified
  raw clipping and completed operation; no source summary unless ingestion was requested.
- **Format or service capture:** read the matching complete route:
  [PDF](references/clip-pdf.md), [Word](references/clip-docx.md),
  [PowerPoint](references/clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheets](references/clip-xlsx.md),
  [GitHub repository](references/clip-gh.md), or [Confluence](references/clip-confluence.md).
  Request: “Clip this PDF with its figures.” Action: run its linked prerequisite
  check, then `clip-pdf.mjs --figures` inside the owned operation and inspect the
  returned text/images. Result: citable capture paths with actual fidelity limits.
  Other formats use their named helper, never an improvised raw file.
- **Named ingestion:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md).
  Request: “Ingest these two clippings.” Action: read exactly those sources,
  exclude restricted or already-summarized hashes, then write only supported
  source/concept changes. Result: summaries with exact raw paths and source hashes.
- **Default backlog ingestion:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md) and the
  [hash-join contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md).
  Request: “Process new clippings.” Action: obtain the
  [backlog report](../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog), then
  inspect eligibility. Result: only eligible sources are ingested; already summarized
  sources stay unchanged and restricted sources are reported separately. If none
  remain, make no pages, operation, log, commit or index refresh.

## Best practices

Prefer named source sets and coordinate shared concept/catalog edits. A capture's
fidelity and its author's credibility are different judgments. Do not invent
text when tools or authenticated access are unavailable. Source count is not a
quality target. Do not treat a backlog count as ingestion authorization.

## Advanced references

Load the exact [capture prerequisite section](../wiki-setup/references/capture-prerequisites.md)
the selected format requires. Tool trouble uses that same section; operation
failure uses [recovery](../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md). Concept
identity, evidence and transaction rules remain in the directly linked shared
contracts; original project documentation belongs to [wiki-project](../wiki-project/SKILL.md).

## Done

The requested candidates, captures or eligible ingestion set are accounted for,
fidelity/exclusions/coverage are honest, and all authorized mutations have exact
ledgers and verified completion. A requested retrieval handoff actually ran.
Candidates-only and zero-eligible ingestion leave the vault unchanged.

# Discover, capture and ingest evidence

Keep the source set and authorized outcome explicit. Candidates-only discovery
is read-only; capture-only creates raw evidence, never derived pages. An
unspecified request to use this role does not authorize processing the backlog.

## Workflow

1. Read [access](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md), resolve the known vault
   and absolute installed helpers, and open applicable vault instructions.
   Choose discovery, named capture, named ingestion or default-backlog ingestion
   from the request. Clarify an ambiguous task before writing.
2. Follow the corresponding direct procedure below. Discovery requires separate
   read-only finders and independent selection when delegation is available;
   retain that selection before capture. Named sources skip broad discovery.
   Ingestion determines eligibility before opening any operation.
3. Read [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md) before judging
   fidelity or synthesizing. Preserve raw bodies, exact hashes and paths,
   restricted-source exclusions and separate Reddit/Medium sections. Before an
   authorized write, read [operation completion](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md),
   open or reuse its token, and record every written path.
4. Capture with the matching helper; pass the same research topic and `--since`
   token throughout a run. Ingest only the authorized eligible set, reuse
   canonical pages and explain useful relationships under the
   [identity contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md).
5. Verify capture fidelity or derived claims, refresh affected owned catalogs and
   log once. Before closing any ingestion, export and inspect its actual owned-path
   ledger, then run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/validate-authored.mjs" --paths-file <ledger>`
   using the direct [scoped validation procedure](../wiki-setup/references/validation.md).
   Require exit 0 before commit/sync; a health, lint or backlog report does not
   replace this validation. Then complete scoped publication unless held.
6. If the request continues with a search or answer, load
   [wiki-search](../wiki-search/SKILL.md) and actually run retrieval against the
   updated vault, opening its returned passages. Use
   [advanced retrieval](../wiki-search/references/advanced.md) or
   [cited answers](../wiki-search/references/answers.md) as needed. Memory of pages
   just written is not retrieval; lexical-only availability is disclosed, not a
   reason to skip this step. The answer stays read-only unless filing is authorized.

## Modes and examples

- **Discover:** read [discovery](references/discover.md).
  Request: “Find evidence on retry budgets; return candidates only.” Action:
  check coverage/dedup, dispatch five perspective finders and independently select
  their candidates. Result: a justified source list without clips, declines or logs.
  An explicit discover-and-capture/ingest request can continue within that scope.
- **Named URL or saved page:** read [capture](references/capture.md).
  Request: “Capture this saved article.” Action: use `clip.mjs --from-file` for
  the named URL, preserving dedup, declines and provenance. Result: a verified
  raw clipping and completed operation; no source summary unless ingestion was requested.
- **Format or service capture:** read the matching complete route:
  [PDF](references/clip-pdf.md), [Word](references/clip-docx.md),
  [PowerPoint](references/clip-pptx.md), [spreadsheets](references/clip-xlsx.md),
  [GitHub repository](references/clip-gh.md), or [Confluence](references/clip-confluence.md).
  Request: “Clip this PDF with its figures.” Action: run its linked prerequisite
  check, then `clip-pdf.mjs --figures` inside the owned operation and inspect the
  returned text/images. Result: citable capture paths with actual fidelity limits.
  Other formats use their named helper, never an improvised raw file.
- **Named ingestion:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md).
  Request: “Ingest these two clippings.” Action: read exactly those sources,
  exclude restricted or already-summarized hashes, then write only supported
  source/concept changes. Result: summaries with exact raw paths and source hashes.
- **Default backlog ingestion:** read [ingestion](references/ingest.md) and the
  [hash-join contract](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md).
  Request: “Process new clippings.” Action: obtain the
  [backlog report](../wiki-setup/references/checks.md#health-and-ingest-backlog), then
  inspect eligibility. Result: only eligible sources are ingested; already summarized
  sources stay unchanged and restricted sources are reported separately. If none
  remain, make no pages, operation, log, commit or index refresh.

## Best practices

Prefer named source sets and coordinate shared concept/catalog edits. A capture's
fidelity and its author's credibility are different judgments. Do not invent
text when tools or authenticated access are unavailable. Source count is not a
quality target. Do not treat a backlog count as ingestion authorization.

## Advanced references

Load the exact [capture prerequisite section](../wiki-setup/references/capture-prerequisites.md)
the selected format requires. Tool trouble uses that same section; operation
failure uses [recovery](../wiki-setup/references/operation-recovery.md). Concept
identity, evidence and transaction rules remain in the directly linked shared
contracts; original project documentation belongs to [wiki-project](../wiki-project/SKILL.md).

## Done

The requested candidates, captures or eligible ingestion set are accounted for,
fidelity/exclusions/coverage are honest, and all authorized mutations have exact
ledgers and verified completion. A requested retrieval handoff actually ran.
Candidates-only and zero-eligible ingestion leave the vault unchanged.

3	
4	# Discover sources on a topic
5	
6	Given a topic, find and independently assess sources that fill an evidence gap.
7	Perspective passes return candidates and never write the vault. A candidates-only
8	request stays read-only: report the selection without declines or captures. When
9	capture is within scope, use [capture and completion](capture.md#capture-the-selected-sources).
10	Ingestion is a separate authorized mode.
11	
12	## Independence checkpoint before capture
13	
14	Topic discovery requires the five perspective passes below and independent
15	selection. When the host provides delegation, actually dispatch read-only
16	finders; do not replace their execution with a list you found and scored yourself.
17	The orchestrator may select their returned candidates, or a separate reviewer
18	may select them. A finder must not grade its own finds. A small or controlled
19	source corpus does not remove this separation.
20	
21	Before opening an operation or calling a clipper, retain the returned candidate
22	lists and the independent selection with its credibility reasons. If delegation
23	is unavailable, use the documented sequential lenses and disclose that limit;
24	do not claim an independent pass that did not run. Named-source capture skips
25	topic discovery and uses [capture](capture.md) directly.
26	
27	## Phase 0 — dedup before searching
28	Gather what the wiki already has so the search hunts for *gaps*, not dupes:
29	- Known source URLs: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/known-urls.mjs"` prints
30	  them, one per line, normalized as the clipper normalizes them (`--count` prints
31	  the number). It reads the clippings themselves (the first `source:` line of each
32	  file directly under `raw/clippings`), rather than querying an index built from
33	  them — the shortest path to the fact, and it stays correct while the index is
34	  stale. To ask about particular candidates, use
35	  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/known-urls.mjs" --check "<url>" "<url>"`: one line
36	  per URL, in the order given, `new`, `clipped raw/clippings/<name>.md` (with
37	  ` (+N recapture)` when later captures of the page exist) or `declined: <reason>`.
38	  `--summary --topic "<topic>"` prints what a topic already holds. All three only read.
39	- Coverage summary: name the unanswered question, run bounded wiki searches, and
40	  read the relevant task MOC and leading concept/synthesis pages. Read only the
41	  manual Start here section of `index.md` if orientation is needed; do not load
42	  the generated catalog. List the known coverage and the specific evidence gap.
43	- Sanity-check the set: if the vault has clippings on disk but the known-URL
44	  set is empty, STOP — the collection step failed; do not proceed to search.
45	Pass the known-URL set + a one-line "already covered" summary to every perspective.
46	
47	## Phase 1 — five perspective researchers (parallel if supported, else sequential)
48	Each perspective gets: the topic, the known-URL set, the coverage summary, and its
49	lens. Run them **in parallel if your host supports agent fan-out** — Claude Code:
50	dispatch five read-only agents in one message via the Agent tool; Copilot CLI: use
51	custom agents — **otherwise run the five lenses sequentially yourself.** Each runs
52	2–3 *varied* web searches, pre-skips any result whose domain is on the blocklist,
53	fetches the promising hits, and **returns a ranked candidate list** — it writes
54	nothing. Lenses:
55	- **Academic** — papers, textbooks, primary research, .edu.
56	- **Technical** — official docs, specs, standards, source repos.
57	- **Applied** — case studies, real-world usage, tutorials from practitioners.
58	- **News/Trends** — recent developments, reputable reporting (last ~2 years).
59	- **Contrarian** — critiques, failure modes, dissenting analysis.
60	
61	Each candidate: `{ title, url, quality_guess: high|medium|low, key_findings,

# Discover sources on a topic

Given a topic, find and independently assess sources that fill an evidence gap.
Perspective passes return candidates and never write the vault. A candidates-only
request stays read-only: report the selection without declines or captures. When
capture is within scope, use [capture and completion](capture.md#capture-the-selected-sources).
Ingestion is a separate authorized mode.

## Independence checkpoint before capture

Topic discovery requires the five perspective passes below and independent
selection. When the host provides delegation, actually dispatch read-only
finders; do not replace their execution with a list you found and scored yourself.
The orchestrator may select their returned candidates, or a separate reviewer
may select them. A finder must not grade its own finds. A small or controlled
source corpus does not remove this separation.

Before opening an operation or calling a clipper, retain the returned candidate
lists and the independent selection with its credibility reasons. If delegation
is unavailable, use the documented sequential lenses and disclose that limit;
do not claim an independent pass that did not run. Named-source capture skips
topic discovery and uses [capture](capture.md) directly.

## Phase 0 — dedup before searching
Gather what the wiki already has so the search hunts for *gaps*, not dupes:
- Known source URLs: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/known-urls.mjs"` prints
  them, one per line, normalized as the clipper normalizes them (`--count` prints
  the number). It reads the clippings themselves (the first `source:` line of each
  file directly under `raw/clippings`), rather than querying an index built from
  them — the shortest path to the fact, and it stays correct while the index is
  stale. To ask about particular candidates, use
  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/known-urls.mjs" --check "<url>" "<url>"`: one line
  per URL, in the order given, `new`, `clipped raw/clippings/<name>.md` (with
  ` (+N recapture)` when later captures of the page exist) or `declined: <reason>`.
  `--summary --topic "<topic>"` prints what a topic already holds. All three only read.
- Coverage summary: name the unanswered question, run bounded wiki searches, and
  read the relevant task MOC and leading concept/synthesis pages. Read only the
  manual Start here section of `index.md` if orientation is needed; do not load
  the generated catalog. List the known coverage and the specific evidence gap.
- Sanity-check the set: if the vault has clippings on disk but the known-URL
  set is empty, STOP — the collection step failed; do not proceed to search.
Pass the known-URL set + a one-line "already covered" summary to every perspective.

## Phase 1 — five perspective researchers (parallel if supported, else sequential)
Each perspective gets: the topic, the known-URL set, the coverage summary, and its
lens. Run them **in parallel if your host supports agent fan-out** — Claude Code:
dispatch five read-only agents in one message via the Agent tool; Copilot CLI: use
custom agents — **otherwise run the five lenses sequentially yourself.** Each runs
2–3 *varied* web searches, pre-skips any result whose domain is on the blocklist,
fetches the promising hits, and **returns a ranked candidate list** — it writes
nothing. Lenses:
- **Academic** — papers, textbooks, primary research, .edu.
- **Technical** — official docs, specs, standards, source repos.
- **Applied** — case studies, real-world usage, tutorials from practitioners.
- **News/Trends** — recent developments, reputable reporting (last ~2 years).
- **Contrarian** — critiques, failure modes, dissenting analysis.

Each candidate: `{ title, url, quality_guess: high|medium|low, key_findings,
why_ingest, adds_evidence, changes_page }`. `adds_evidence` names the unanswered
question it helps settle; `changes_page` names an existing or proposed concept
or synthesis. More material on an already answered question is not automatically
an improvement. Inspect existing high-use stubs and missing bridges before
requesting another broad collection run.

  `--quality=<tier>` and `--since <token>` on every clip.
- A page the user rejects is recorded, not forgotten:
  `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --decline="<one-line reason>"`.
- Use the capture and completion contract below: open a discover operation
  before the first decline or clip, pass its token as `--since`, finish the capture
  with `op-ledger.mjs show` and `op-commit`. Ingest only when the exact source set
  is already authorized; a capture-only request ends after verified capture publication.
- A page the clipper cannot read (a login, a consent wall, an age check, a thin
  extraction) is saved by the user from a signed-in browser and supplied with
  `--from-file` (below).

## Capture the selected sources
Use the operation opened before the first decline or clip. If none is open, run
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op discover` before clipping
and retain its token; never overwrite a saved token. Do prerequisite and duplicate
checks first. When there is nothing to capture or decline, return without opening
an operation. Read-only named-URL dedup does not require broad coverage research.

For each kept candidate:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip.mjs" "<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>`

**Pass `--topic` on every clip in the run, and use the same string for all of
them** — it is what lets maintainer triage group this run's leftovers together
later. Use the topic as the user gave it ($ARGUMENTS); do not re-word it per
source, or one run becomes several groups. The flag feeds both places a topic
can land: the clipping's frontmatter when the clip succeeds, and the triage log
when it fails, so you never have to know which happened.

**"Every clip" includes the non-HTML ones.** A candidate that is a PDF, a Word
file or a spreadsheet does not go through `clip.mjs` — it goes through
`clip-pdf.mjs`, `clip-docx.mjs` or `clip-xlsx.mjs` (see [PDF capture](clip-pdf.md) and
[Word capture](clip-docx.md)), and **every one of those takes `--topic` too**:

```bash
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-pdf.mjs"  "<file.pdf>"  --source="<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-docx.mjs" "<file.docx>" --source="<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-xlsx.mjs" "<file.xlsx>" --source="<url>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
# clip-pptx.mjs takes the same options; clip-pdf also records the figure files it renders (--figures)
```

**A Confluence Cloud URL is HTML but also does not go through `clip.mjs`** — it
requires authentication `clip.mjs`'s anonymous fetch does not have, and reads
as thin content / gets auto-declined. Route it to [Confluence capture](clip-confluence.md) instead
(only applies if the `confluencer` plugin is installed — an optional runtime
dependency this one clipper alone takes on; see that reference for why):

```bash
node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/clip-confluence.mjs" "<confluence-url-or-page-id>" --quality=<tier> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>
```

Binary capture routes need the same topic string as HTML routes. Topic is
recorded going forward only; missing attribution leaves the resulting rows under
Unattributed. For a one-off named source outside a research run, omit the topic
rather than inventing one.

It blocks unreliable domains, skips dupes, extracts via Defuddle, and writes
`raw/clippings/<slug>.md` with `source`, `created`, `tags:[clippings]`, `quality`,
`topic`, `source-hash`. Read the actual outcome: automatic thin declines differ
from transient failures and wrong-node walls, which are queued rather than judged
as sources. Use [HTML/supplied-page diagnosis](../../wiki-setup/references/capture-prerequisites.md#html-and-supplied-pages) for thin, wrong-node, transient, clash or supplied-file refusal recovery; do not retry blindly or fabricate a raw file.

A raw text URL (for example a checksum manifest or pinned source file) is captured whole in a code fence with `extraction: plaintext`, without the ordinary thin-content test. Binary/oversized refusal diagnosis remains in the directly linked setup procedure.

**What a clip result means.** `clip.mjs` prints one result per URL:

| Result | Meaning | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| `clipped: raw/clippings/<name>.md` | written | cite that path |
| `duplicate (already clipped)` | this URL is already in the vault, also when another session wrote it first | nothing; do not clip it again. To keep a second, dated copy of a page that has changed, run the clip again with `--recapture` |
| `unchanged (same text as raw/clippings/<name>.md); nothing written` | `--recapture` found the page's text identical to a capture already held (exit 0) | nothing; the page has not changed |
| `recapture: not clipped yet, clipping it normally: <url>` | `--recapture` on a URL that was not in the vault; the line is followed by the ordinary result | read the result that follows |
| `clash: <url>: raw/clippings/<name>.md already exists ...` | the URL is new but every name it could have had was taken; **nothing was written** and one `attention` row is queued in triage | follow [clash diagnosis](../../wiki-setup/references/capture-prerequisites.md#html-and-supplied-pages) or leave the row for maintainer triage |
| `declined`, `blocked`, `thin content`, `failed` | no successful capture | use [outcome diagnosis](../../wiki-setup/references/capture-prerequisites.md#html-and-supplied-pages); report the actual result |

A taken file name is a `clash`, never a `duplicate`: a `duplicate` always means the same URL.

**A second capture of a page already clipped.** `clip.mjs "<url>" --recapture --since <token>` fetches the page and runs the usual checks. If the text is new it writes a second clipping beside the first, named as the oldest capture's own name followed by ` (recaptured YYYY-MM-DD)`, with the same suffix on its `title`, `recapture-of` naming the newest existing capture, and `created` today; the older clipping is never edited. A second recapture on the same day with different text is a `clash`. `--slug=<name>` with `--recapture` is used exactly, with no suffix. Without the flag the same URL is a `duplicate`.

**A page a person saved.** `clip.mjs "<url>" --from-file <path> --topic="<topic>" --since <token>` records a page saved from a signed-in browser, with its real URL as `source` and nothing fetched. The file is `.md`, `.markdown` or `.txt` (the page text) or `.html` or `.htm` (read by the same extractor as a fetched page), at most 1 MiB. The clipping carries `extraction: manual` and `supplied-sha256`, the SHA-256 of the file's bytes; the file's name is not recorded. The ordinary thin, interstitial and decline checks still apply; inspect the actual result and [supplied-page diagnosis](../../wiki-setup/references/capture-prerequisites.md#html-and-supplied-pages). `--from-file` on an existing URL is a duplicate; adding `--recapture` requests a dated new capture. Refresh an `extraction: manual` clipping through this same supplied-file route, not `apply-reclips`. These interfaces do not authorize inventing the page body.

**Names.** A page's title names its file. A document with no title and no heading is named from its URL path, nearest folder first, so `.../skills/one/SKILL.md` is `one-SKILL.md` and `.../skills/two/SKILL.md` is `two-SKILL.md`; the bare last segment is used only after the folders. The frontmatter `title:` stays exactly what the extractor returned, so `title: ""` on such a clipping is not a defect. A new clipping never ends `.md.md`; an older one may, and its name is still valid. A title another clipping already holds gets the distinguishing URL part added, for example `Smith v. Jones (93-1260.ZO)`. `--slug=<name>` chooses the file name without `.md`; a taken name is a clash and is never suffixed. `clip-pdf`, `clip-docx`, `clip-pptx` and `clip-xlsx` also take `--title="<text>"`, for a file whose name is not its title (`valve.pdf`), and `--slug=<name>`.

An option a clipper does not know exits 2 with its usage and clips nothing; `--help` prints the usage and clips nothing.

**Every unresolved link is queued for triage automatically.** `clip.mjs` records
`failed`, `thin`, and `wrong-node` outcomes to `.wiki-master/triage.jsonl`, so a
link that needs a human survives the terminal scrollback. Do not rely on your
completion report to carry them — point the user at [maintainer triage](../../wiki-maintainer/references/triage.md), where they can
disposition each one (retry, decline, clipped-by-hand). Queue anything else that
needs their judgement yourself with `recordIssue(vaultPath, { url, kind:
'attention', reason })`.

## Finish capture and report
Show the ranked list (title, url, quality, why), which clips succeeded, and which
were skipped (blocked, duplicate, thin, failed). If issues were queued, mention
maintainer triage and report their counts.

**Finish the capture operation before any decision pause.** The clipping set is what
the clippers recorded, not something to rebuild afterwards: run
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" show --since <saved-token> --out <ledger>`
and read its `raw/clippings/...` entries, exactly as written (a name with an em dash
included). The number of `raw/clippings/` entries must equal the number of clippings the
`clipped:` results reported (one per URL or file; `clip-gh` reports a file count, and
`clip-pdf --figures` adds `raw/figures/` entries that are not clippings); if it does not,
stop and find the difference. Never rebuild the set from `git show`, whose default output
quotes and escapes a non-ASCII name. Write one discovery log entry naming the
clipped/declined/failed counts (`log-entry.mjs ... --since <saved-token>`), run `show`
again, and close with:
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op discover --title "<topic> → N clipped" --since <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger>`.
Validate any derived pages written during the authorized task through [scoped validation](../../wiki-setup/references/validation.md), and verify raw capture paths and fidelity before close.
The `<ledger>` file you wrote outlives the close, so the ingest that follows takes its
clipping set from it.
Without `--paths-file` the close is refused while another operation is open. Verify the commit and push and verify remote publication through the shared
contract (`wiki-sync.mjs --op <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "<topic>"` closes and pushes in one command). If no writes occurred, report that and do not manufacture a log/commit.
Clippings must not remain dirty while waiting for an ingestion decision.

Then use the existing authorization for this exact source set:
- **Discover-and-ingest already authorized:** read [ingestion](ingest.md) and process the named
  successful clippings immediately. It owns a fresh operation and its own log.
  No second confirmation is needed.
- **Only discovery or capture authorized:** report the captured set and stop; do
  not create derived pages. If ingestion is subsequently requested, use the named
  set in a fresh operation.
- **Ingestion declined:** retain the committed clippings for manual review.

## Guardrails
- The perspective passes never write the vault; the matching clipping helper is the sole writer to its raw artifacts.
- Never edit the **body** of anything under `raw/` — clipped content is immutable
  source-of-truth. Frontmatter is pipeline state and may be updated by wiki-master
  tooling only (never by hand, never the body).
- Prefer primary/authoritative sources over open-publishing platforms.
- Ingestion requires authorization for this scope; existing explicit authorization
  satisfies this ingestion boundary. Do not add another confirmation to an approved discover-and-ingest run.
